caption: The drawing depicts a formal garden layout viewed from above, characterized by a symmetrical rectangular composition. The garden is divided into multiple long, narrow rectangular and curved sections, bordered by green strips that represent grass or hedges. Central to the design is an oval-shaped fountain or water feature, illustrated in pale blue and white, located slightly above the horizontal midpoint. Surrounding the fountain are pathways, depicted in a tan or buff color, which run both horizontally and vertically, segmenting the planting beds. The planting beds themselves are filled with various colors: red, pink, blue, purple, and white, suggesting different flower types or patterns, with some beds displaying wavy lines and swirls of alternating color. Around the perimeter of the main rectangular area, blocks of solid green indicate grass expanses. The outermost margin of the paper is a light tan, with signs of age and wear at the edges. At the bottom center, blue text reads: "THE J.W. WOOD PARTERRE - THE BLACKWELL SURVEY 1860".
title: Parterre - J. W. Wood
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
